## 2026-11-14 - M11 step 5: the compositor pauses for programs that write straight to the screen, and the forced failure ends in the CPU mode

Problem: a `BDirectWindow` with direct access and a `BWindowScreen` write the front buffer, which the compositor also writes. Decision 9 asks for a pause, the CPU-mode way, and a resume when the last direct access ends; decision 11 for a forced failure that ends in the CPU mode.

What changed:
- Compositor: `IsActive()` is false while paused, `IsEnabled()` stays true for the session; everything in Desktop, Window and ServerWindow that asks `IsActive()` takes the CPU-mode path by itself. A compose slot is held for one frame; the compose thread never takes the window lock while holding it (a failed compose is handled at the top of the loop, outside the slot). Lock order: `fWindowLock` (write) → compose slot → `HWInterface`.
- Pause: `ServerWindow::HandleDirectConnection()` with `B_DIRECT_START`, before `SetState()`, and `Desktop::LockDirectScreen()`: waits for the compose in flight, rebinds every engine to the screen, drops the layers and animations, `app_server: compositor paused: direct window`; the compose thread then redraws the desktop the CPU-mode way once the caller's write lock is released.
- Resume: when no window has direct access and no team holds the direct screen, the compose thread (under `LockAllWindows()`) rebinds the engines to their buffers, rebuilds the clipping, lets every window draw once, `app_server: compositor resumed`. Moving a direct window (stop and start under one write lock) neither resumes nor pauses.
- Windows made during a pause still get a window buffer, and draw to the screen until the resume. Shares (3b) can still be offered during a pause.
- The switch to the CPU mode and a device that goes away give every shared image app_server holds back to its program, so none waits in its acquire.
- A `BWindowScreen` program that ended (killed) with the screen held kept the direct screen lock, and the compositor paused, for good; its `ServerApp` thread now gives the lock back when its loop ends. (In Haiku the lock stayed taken too.)
- `Desktop::LockDirectScreen()` pauses first (window lock) and takes the direct screen lock after: `_SetCurrentWorkspaceConfiguration()` takes the two the other way round, with a 1 s timeout after which it stops the program. A lock that times out while another team holds the screen keeps the pause.

Mistakes and fixes during this step: two members out of initialisation order (`-Werror=reorder`); my first boot-A script had the wrong VulkanTeapot path (`/system/bin/VulkanTeapot`) and planted the two test programs without execute rights for the session user. A killed ParticlesII left the compositor paused (above), found in the first boot and fixed.

Tested (QEMU, KVM, Lavapipe, 14 Nov 2026), copies of the image with `gpu_compositor true` and `gpu_debug true`, effects off so the compare runs:
- Chart (Haiku demo, `BDirectWindow`), Display "DirectWindow", Slow rotation at 60 frames/s, dragged twice by its tab (QMP), closed: one `compositor paused: direct window` when it opened, one `compositor resumed` when it closed, nothing for the drags; `compose compare ok` 6 times after. A second boot with VulkanTeapot open: the same pair; VulkanTeapot kept rotating during and after the pause.
- `BWindowScreen`: Haiku's own tests ParticlesII and PageFlipper (`src/tests/kits/game`, planted in the test copy only, not in the image). ParticlesII killed while holding the screen: paused, then `resumed` at the kill (after the fix). PageFlipper: paused and resumed in the same second (it gives the screen back at once in QEMU). The same again after the lock-order change: `compose compare ok` 12 times, no crash.
- Without settings: no line containing `compositor` in the whole syslog, no crash.
- `compose compare ok` 11 times in the BWindowScreen boot, never `MISMATCH`.

The forced failure first crashed (stopped after two tries in the night run): with `gpu_compositor_fail true` app_server crashed a few seconds into the boot. A new app_server thread (`a:186:x-vnd.Haiku-notification_`) got a segment violation in the runtime loader's TLS copy (`TLSBlockTemplates::Materialize`). Keeping app_server's own `dlopen` handles did not help (tried, undone). The cause, found in a read-only review (Gemini) and checked in the source: the switch to the CPU mode destroys the Vulkan instance, the Vulkan loader unloads Lavapipe (Mesa uses thread-local storage), and R5's static TLS code in the runtime loader (`elf_tls.cpp`, an R5 snippet) kept the unloaded library's template in `TLSBlockTemplates::Unregister()`. Every thread started after that copied from unmapped memory. It was not a race, and not only app_server: any program that unloads a library with thread-local storage and then starts a thread crashed the same way. Fix: `Unregister()` clears the template, so `Materialize()` skips it. This turn-off path is from step 2 and had never run; it is the same path a real failed submit or a lost device without restart takes.

Tested after the fix (QEMU, KVM, Lavapipe, 14 Nov 2026), jam rc 0. Copy with `gpu_compositor true`, `gpu_debug true` and `gpu_compositor_fail true`: `gpu compositor on lavapipe: no render node`, then exactly one `app_server: gpu compositor off: forced failure` in the same second, no crash anywhere in the syslog; Sign in, Deskbar, Tracker and Terminal worked; VulkanTeapot presented 65159 frames, all `vkQueueWaitIdle 0`, over the 90 s of the session (its window was under Terminal, so the picture itself was not checked); clean shutdown. Copy without the forced failure: Chart opened → `compositor paused: direct window`, closed → `compositor resumed` (same seconds as the test marks), `compose compare ok` twice, no `MISMATCH`, no crash.

Seen: in the BWindowScreen boot one `draw outside buffer: Deskbar` line, because `BWindowScreen` sets its screen mode before it takes the screen lock (the safety check caught it; not drawn). VulkanTeapot's copy path shows half-drawn frames (white bands) now and then, in the CPU mode as well as composed; not from this step.

Not tested: RADV on the 5625U (shared images during a pause, the scanout copy with the pause), VirtualBox, a `BDirectWindow` that never asks for direct access (in Haiku every `BDirectWindow` gets direct access when shown).

## 2026-11-13 - Three old check failures fixed: the WSI ioctl, guilty after a reset, the share check name

Symbol check: `scripts/check-libdrm-symbols.py` rejected `__ioctl` request 30479 in `libvulkan_radeon.so` and `libvulkan_lvp.so` since M10. That is `R5_GPU_GET_INFO` in `r5_gpu_available` of the R5 WSI (`distro/mesa/wsi/wsi_common_haiku.cpp`), which reads `R5_GPU_CAP_AVAILABLE` before RADV may present. R5 code may read the R5 GPU interface directly, and it is not a Linux DRM request that `drmIoctl` would translate, so the use is correct. The check now allows that request only in that one function (`ALLOWED_IOCTL_IN`, by symbol name); `SYNC_IOC_MERGE` stays allowed everywhere as before, and everything else still fails. Guilty after a reset: the library test (`scripts/test-r5-libdrm.c`) expected `AMDGPU_CTX_QUERY2_FLAGS_GUILTY` from `AMDGPU_CTX_OP_QUERY_STATE2` when the fake kernel set only `R5_GPU_CAP_LOST`. The test was wrong, not the library: the hang policy (`docs/GRAPHICS.md`, GFX9 reset on GC 9.3) marks every file with a context lost and only the file whose job hung guilty, and since the commit that marks only the hung file guilty `r5_translate.c` reports GUILTY only when `R5_GPU_CAP_GUILTY` is set too (`r5_gpu_query_guilty`). The fake kernel now also has a guilty bit, and the test checks three cases: lost only is RESET with `AMDGPU_CTX_INNOCENT_RESET`, lost and guilty is RESET and GUILTY with `AMDGPU_CTX_GUILTY_RESET`, guilty without lost is no reset. The library, the kernel and the contract are unchanged. A second failure on `main`, `share_libdrm` (`result.alloc_size == 3 * 4096`), came from stale host objects: `scripts/test-ac-drm.sh` ran `ninja` on the host libdrm build only when it had never been built, so the objects in `~/r5os` were from 5 Nov, before the fifth libdrm patch. The script now always runs `ninja` (incremental). Tested on the build host with a copy of `test-ac-drm.sh` that builds the host libdrm objects and the test into a temp folder (the shared tree was not written): before the fix only the guilty check failed; after it `ok ac drm family RV cu 7 firmware map share` and `ok libdrm ioctl`, rc 0. ## 2026-11-13 - M11 step 3b: Vulkan windows without a copy (A2) and the scanout through Vulkan, behind gpu_compositor

Problem: a Vulkan window was copied by the CPU into a `BBitmap` every frame, and the composed screen went through a CPU copy into the back buffer and the M8 `DMA_DATA` copy. Step 3b builds the 3a design (`docs/APP-SERVER-COMPOSITOR.md`, #4251, #4252) and decision 15b.

What changed:
- Kernel (`r5gpu`): `R5_GPU_BO_EXPORT` (`+ 17`) and `R5_GPU_BO_IMPORT` (`+ 18`) work, `R5_GPU_BO_PRESENT_MARK` (`+ 32`) is new (`r5_gpu.h`). A buffer's memory is a backing with a reference count, apart from each file's handle. An export number is a counter times an odd constant plus two `secure_random_value()` words, in an opaque 128-bit field. An import succeeds only for app_server, for the team pinned at export, once, within 5 s; at most 32 pending exports per file, removed with their file and by the watchdog. Slots: 1024, 512 per file, the last 64 only for app_server; `radeon_hd: buffer limit <n> reached, team <id>` once per file. `GET_INFO` `vram_usage`/`gtt_usage` count backings. The logic is `r5_share.h` (pure, host-tested); `apply-radeon.py` copies it.
- R5 DRM library: `PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD`/`PRIME_FD_TO_HANDLE` through export numbers and local `/dev/null` fds; `GEM_OP` (size, domain and flags from `BO_IMPORT`) and `GEM_METADATA` (neutral). New calls, MIT: `r5_drm_fd_to_token` (with an export id), `r5_drm_token_to_fd` (with an import id), `r5_drm_import_bytes`, `r5_drm_mark_get`, `r5_drm_mark_set`, `r5_drm_import_size`. An import is kept by its id, not by the fd number; `GEM_CLOSE` ends it. Fifth libdrm patch `haiku-import-size.patch`: `amdgpu_bo_import` takes the size from the library instead of `lseek`.
- WSI (`wsi_common_haiku.cpp`): on RADV a view swapchain first tries a `WSI_IMAGE_TYPE_DRM` swapchain with three linear, exported buffers (prime path, `same_gpu = false`), one free semaphore per image, the present mark before each present, and its own `AppServerLink` (no change in libbe). New link codes `AS_R5_SHARE_IMAGES`, `_PRESENT`, `_END` at the end of an R5 copy of `ServerProtocol.h` (`distro/rest`). A refusal keeps the `BBitmap` copy path; Lavapipe says it does not share. An acquire timeout is `VK_TIMEOUT`.
- app_server: `ServerApp` finds the view by its token in that application's token space; the team for `BO_IMPORT` is the connection's. The compositor imports each image (RADV only), refuses a semaphore of another team (`zero-copy off: sem`) and a size the kernel does not back (`zero-copy off: size`, through `r5_drm_import_size`, 64-bit), and draws the current image over its window. A presented image is shown once `FENCE_WAIT` with timeout 0 says the ring passed its mark; until then the previous one stays and the view is composed again next period. The image it replaces goes back with `release_sem_etc`.
- Scanout (decision 4, own commit, `gpu_compositor_scanout true`, off by default): the frame is `GPUCopy`'s GTT back buffer; `GPUCopy` exports it and the scanout to app_server itself, the compositor imports both, and one `vkCmdCopyBuffer` of the damaged rows (each buffer's own pitch) runs in the compose submit. After the fence `InvalidateRegion` only draws the cursor (`GPUCopy::FrontCurrent`, per thread). A mode change imports again before the next compose. `gpu_debug` logs `present median <us> (vulkan|cpu)`.
- `r5-share-check` (in the image next to `r5-wsi-test`): an import by a program that is not app_server, the same number offered twice, and `hold`/`count` for the stick script with `kill`.

Decided during this step (user, 13 Nov 2026; "Decided in step 3b" in the design): the present mark through library ids on both sides; `r5_drm_import_size` for app_server's size check; the frame is the back buffer (option A); an acquire timeout is `VK_TIMEOUT`; the refusal rules are host-test cases and the machine runs a short check, the stuck job is `gpu_hang_test`.

The calling team must now also run with effective uid 0 (`geteuid()`); the path stays the second check (`r5_share_compositor_caller`, host-tested; `r5-share-check` runs a copy of itself with argv[0] set to app_server's path as a user and expects `B_NOT_ALLOWED`). ## 2026-11-13 - M11 step 2: the compositor core (A1), behind gpu_compositor

Problem: M11 composes the desktop on the GPU. Step 2 is the core: one buffer per window, a compose with Vulkan, the fallback, and the compare and measurement of decision 7 and 14.

What changed:
- New in `distro/app_server` (MIT): `Compositor` (Vulkan loaded at run time; RADV when `R5_GPU_CAP_AVAILABLE` is set, otherwise Lavapipe, otherwise the CPU mode), `WindowBuffer`, `WindowHWInterface`, the shader `compositor/compose.comp` and its generated `compositor_shaders.h` (`scripts/gen-compositor-shaders.sh`, glslang 16.6.0 on the build host). Off unless `gpu_compositor true` in the radeon_hd settings, read the way the M8 copy reads `gpu_app_server`.
- Every window draws into its own Vulkan buffer (host-visible, coherent, host-cached first; decision 5), through its own `WindowHWInterface`. Painter is unchanged: it gets a view of the buffer whose address is screen pixel (0, 0) (user's choice, "Decided in step 2").
- **Covered parts are drawn ("Decided after step 0", point 1):** in the GPU mode a window draws all of itself, also what other windows cover, and also outside an update (`Window::DrawableRegion()`). When a window above goes away, what is below is already right. Programs that draw outside an update draw a little more.
- Moving a window: no blit, no redraw of the windows below; the compose puts the window at its new place. A resize gets a new buffer with the old pixels copied by screen position.
- The compose: only on damage, at most once per refresh period of the display mode; one compute dispatch per damaged rectangle, back to front; then the damage goes through the screen's back buffer and `CopyBackToFront` (CPU row copy on Lavapipe, the M8 `DMA_DATA` copy on RADV when `gpu_app_server` is on).
- Decision 14: a late fence is not a failure (`compose late <n> ms`); a failed submit or a lost device ends the GPU mode (`gpu compositor off: <reason>`), with one restart on RADV after a successful reset. `gpu_compositor_fail true` makes the first submit fail.
- `gpu_debug true`: every 100th frame (and the first) is composed again on the CPU from the same buffers and compared (`compose compare ok` / `MISMATCH at x,y`); every 10 s `compose median <n> us cpu <n> ms per 10 s` and `window memory <n> MB`. At start: `vulkan queue family <i> flags <hex>` per family (a family with the graphics bit is used, decision 16) and, at the first window buffer, `window memory type <i> flags <hex>`.
- Memory budget (half the GTT on RADV, a quarter of RAM on Lavapipe): buffers of windows not on screen are freed first, the one shown longest ago first; a window on screen that cannot get a buffer ends the GPU mode (`window memory`).
- glslang 16.6.0 is in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `docs/LICENSING.md` as a build tool (its generated parser is GPL-3.0-or-later WITH Bison-exception-2.2; nothing of it ships).

Mistakes and fixes during this step:
- app_server crashed in `Painter::StraightLine` while Deskbar (created at -1000,-1000) and the notification window (at x -4) drew their border. First the Painter view became invalid for a window fully off the left or top, and Painter kept its old buffer; fixed by keeping the view valid. Then the real cause, found with temporary serial diagnostics: Painter multiplies a row by an unsigned stride, so it cannot draw at a negative coordinate. `Window::_ClipToBuffer` now limits every drawable region to the window's buffer and to x >= 0, y >= 0, and logs `draw outside buffer` once per window if a region ever reaches past the buffer. A part off the left or top is drawn when it comes on screen.
- The first interactive test ran without the compositor: the settings file was written to a WSL `/tmp` that was emptied between two calls. The test was repeated with the setting checked in the image.
- Two inserted log strings got a real newline instead of the `\n` escape; fixed before building.

Tested (QEMU, KVM, usernet, Lavapipe, 13 Nov 2026), copy A with `gpu_compositor true` and `gpu_debug true`: `app_server: vulkan queue family 0 flags 0x7`, `app_server: gpu compositor on lavapipe: no render node`, `app_server: window memory type 0 flags 0xf`, `compose late 100 ms` twice (the first frames), `compose compare ok` 21 times, never `MISMATCH`, never `draw outside buffer`, no crash. Measured: `compose median` 4647 to 5302 us, cpu 572 to 613 ms per 10 s, window memory 8 MB. The user ran the test card: Pulse, ActivityMonitor and Clock half covered and then uncovered (correct at once), dragging past the left edge, resizing from the edges, switching workspace; all worked. Copy B without the setting: a full boot log with no line containing `compositor`.

Not tested: RADV and the M8 copy after the compose (needs the 5625U), decision 14 on RADV (late fence under load, reset and restart), `gpu_compositor_fail`, the memory budget when it is exceeded (512 MB in QEMU was not reached), outline resize with `B_OUTLINE_RESIZE` specifically, VirtualBox.

## 2026-11-13 - AMD processors load their microcode update again

Problem: on the Ryzen 5 5625U every thread logged `find_microcode_amd incorrect alignment` and `no fw update found for this cpu`, so the CPU kept the BIOS microcode (`0xa50000f`). The matching patch in `microcode_amd_fam19h.bin` (equiv `a500`, 5568 bytes) starts at an offset that is 4 mod 16, and the loader skipped any patch that was not 16-byte aligned.

What changed (`distro/kernel/src/system/kernel/arch/x86/arch_cpu.cpp`):
- A patch that is not aligned is copied into one 16-byte aligned buffer that lives as long as the kernel, the way Linux copies a patch out of the container before loading it (`arch/x86/kernel/cpu/microcode/amd.c`). It is read only through that pointer, also by the other threads.
- A thread that already reports the new level (the second thread of a core shares its microcode) logs `already at revision` instead of `update failed`.

Tested on the 5625U (combined stick, 13 Nov, image `d0856ac3bf` = main + this PR): `CPU 0: updated from revision 0xa50000f to 0xa500012`, the other first threads the same, the second threads `already at revision 0xa500012`; boots 1 and 4 PASS. QEMU cannot test it (no microcode under a hypervisor). Not tested: other AMD families.
## 2026-11-13 - Deskbar no longer hangs after an app it started quits (kernel, upstream Haiku fix)

Problem: in QEMU, after closing Terminal or AboutSystem started from Deskbar, Deskbar stopped drawing. Three of its threads (`w>Twitcher`, `w>Deskbar`, `_BMediaRoster_`) used about 52 s CPU each; `strace` showed an endless `block_thread(0x0, 0x0) = B_INTERRUPTED (0 us)`.

Cause: `_user_block_thread()` wrote `B_INTERRUPTED` (or a timeout) into `user_thread->wait_status` when a signal interrupted the wait. libroot's `rw_lock_wait()` (used by `BLooperList` since Haiku b6441edfac) retries on `B_INTERRUPTED` without resetting `wait_status`, so every retry returned at once, and the real wake-up from `_kern_unblock_thread()` was ignored because `wait_status` was no longer positive. One signal (here most likely SIGCHLD when the child app quit) left the waiting threads spinning forever. Upstream Haiku ticket #20020.

What changed: `distro/kernel/src/system/kernel/thread.cpp` takes Haiku `cf3a20899c` (10 Nov 2026, Haiku MIT; an upstream import, not an R5 change): the interrupt or timeout is no longer stored in `wait_status`, and `user_unblock_thread()` refuses a positive status and wakes with `B_OK`.

Tested (QEMU/KVM, not on hardware): a small test (`blocktest`, private syscalls, not in the image) waits like `rw_lock_wait()`, gets SIGUSR1, then is woken. Old image (main at 3958ead4a6): `loops=4692233 result=0x1 FAIL` (wake-up lost, busy loop). Image with the fix: `loops=2 result=0x0 PASS`. The Deskbar hang itself did not reproduce on demand in four tries on the old image (timing-dependent), so the Deskbar result rests on the matching signature (`strace`) and the test above. The test image was jammed without `pin-mesa-packages.sh`, because the shared WSL tree pin holds newer Mesa packages from another branch.

## 2026-11-13 - M10 stick, first run: boot 1 passed, the reset did not come back; Deskbar crash

Stick (13 Nov), image `cursor/m9-m10-stick` at `7ea2f881f2`. Found:
- The isolation client's write faults (`vm fault vmid 4 addr 0000000080000000`), and the faulting job stalls the ring. Before M10 the watchdog declared the device lost (ECANCELED); now it is a hang and a reset, and the client's own 10 s wait returned `B_TIMED_OUT` first. `r5-gpu-isolation` accepts both; the guarantee (owner unchanged) is checked by the parent as before. A fault that stalls the ring still costs a reset: open.
- The reset did not come back, in boot 1 (after the isolation hang) and in boot 2 (`gpu_hang_test 1`): `gpu reset mode2 ok`, then `PSP ring init 0x80020115`, `k0 fail fence`, `gpu off until reboot: reset failed`. Linux v6.12 stops the PSP ring before a reset (`psp_suspend()` -> `psp_v12_0_ring_stop()`: `GFX_CTRL_CMD_ID_DESTROY_RINGS` to `C2PMSG_64`, 20 ms, bit 31). `r5_gfx9_kernel_reset()` now does the same first (`r5_gfx9_psp_ring_stop()`, `radeon_hd: reset psp ring stop ok|timeout <hex>`). The boot path is unchanged. Recorded in the `GFX9 reset on GC 9.3` draft.
- Deskbar crashed twice in boot 2 in `TReplicantTray::LoadAddOn` -> `BMessage::AddString`. Its add-on list `~/config/settings/deskbar/replicants` was 254 bytes with a header that says 321 (cut short by the restart after a save); `Unflatten()` failed and left `fAddOnSettings` half built. Deskbar now reads the file into a message of its own and keeps only paths that load. `read-stick-logs.py` copies that file.
- The card was too short: it did not say plainly to open Terminal and type `check`. Boots 3 and 4 did not run.

## 2026-11-13 - Programs no longer crash on a settings file that was cut short

Problem: on the 5625U, Deskbar crashed at start and media_server at shutdown, both in `BMessage::_AddField`. Their settings files had been cut short by the power button: the file had its new size but old blocks (Deskbar's `replicants`: a header for 22 fields in 254 bytes). `BMessage::Unflatten()` read the header, then a short field table, and returned an error without resetting the message: `field_count` stayed 22 over a half-read table, and the next `Add*()` walked garbage.

What changed: `distro/desktop/src/kits/app/Message.cpp` (Haiku `src/kits/app/Message.cpp`, MIT, copied unchanged, then one R5 snippet): a short read of the field table frees it and resets the header, as the data read right below already did. A program that unflattens a damaged file now gets an empty message and an error, and can go on.

Tested: see the PR (QEMU, a small program that unflattens the real 254-byte file from the stick and then adds a field). Not tested on the 5625U.

## 2026-11-12 - The graphics chip is reset after a hang (M10 steps 5-6, draft, not booted)

**Self-test against a second client (AFTER-M8 item 4).** Cause: the kernel stage wait (`gpu_stage_pace_wait` in `r5_gpu.cpp`) waited for the fence to be *equal* to its own sequence. There is one ring and one fence for every client. On stick 46 boot 1 app_server's copies kept submitting, so by the time the marker looked, the fence was already past its sequence (`kern 314624 fence 314624`) and never equal to it. After 5 s it printed `mark selftest timeout 5000 ms`, though its job had landed. Without app_server's copies (boot 2) nothing passed it, so it saw equality after 1 ms. `skipped, gpu lost` was printed for every stopped series, also when the device was not lost; that is why the GPU looked lost while app_server's submits kept landing: it was not lost. The IB in the dump (`0x210000000`) was app_server's because `sLastIbVa` is shared by every submit; that dump is a log only. The fence slot is not the cause. Fix (also in `generated/gpu-m9/SELFTEST-FINDINGS.md`): the wait is now "at or past" (`r5_fence_reached`); the sequence is 64 bits and only grows, so it does not wrap in practice (at a million jobs a second, after more than 500 000 years), and no wrap handling was added. `skipped, gpu lost` is printed only when the device is lost; otherwise `radeon_hd: p skipped: <step> <timeout|priv|room|build>`. A hang dump of a self-test step names its own indirect buffer (`<step> own ib <va>`), not `sLastIbVa` of another client. The watchdog uses the same test, so a job that a later job already passed is never a hang. Host test: the fence jumps from `sequence - 1` to `sequence + 1` between two polls; the wait ends on the second poll, and the old test never matches.

Shared VMID 1, checked in the code, not on a boot: the self-test pages are at the top of the low range (`R5_GPU_VA_MAX - 0x50000` up to `R5_GPU_VA_MAX - 0x6000`) in the shared VMID 1 tree. `r5_vm_va_fits` does not reserve that range, so a client on VMID 1 could map a buffer there, and the self-test would overwrite and then clear that PTE. libdrm's VA manager hands out the low range from the bottom, and app_server's IB was at `0x210000000`, so this did not happen on stick 46. With `gfx9_vmid_per_file` every file has its own tree and the clash cannot happen. Not changed: reserving the range would change the VA range that `GET_INFO` reports.

**Hang policy.** `r5_hang.h` (MIT) holds one pure function, `r5_hang_step()`: the state and one event (hang, reset ok/failed, self-test ok/failed) give the new state and the actions. The kernel core runs them. First hang: the hang line, every file with a context is lost, mode-2 reset, the fixed GFX9 sequences again in contract order, the kernel self-test (the stage P marker), then new contexts work. Second hang, failed reset or failed self-test: the GPU is off until the next boot; the node refuses contexts and submits, and `GET_INFO` reports `R5_GPU_CAP_LOST` without `R5_GPU_CAP_RENDER`. A lost file gets `ECANCELED` on submits and waits and `CAP_LOST` until it destroys its context; the existing libdrm path turns that into `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`. Lines: `radeon_hd: gpu hang ring gfx seq <n> after <ms> ms`, `radeon_hd: gpu reset mode2 ok|failed`, `radeon_hd: gpu selftest after reset ok|failed`, `radeon_hd: gpu off until reboot: <second hang|reset failed|selftest failed>`. Host test `scripts/test-r5-hang.cpp`: one hang, two hangs, a reset fail, a self-test fail, stray events, a hang while a second client works, and the hang IB.

**Mode-2 reset in the kernel.** `radeon_hd/r5_smu12.cpp` is ported from the MIT Linux v6.12 files `smu_v12_0.c:208-211`, `smu_cmn.c` (`__smu_cmn_poll_stat`, `__smu_cmn_send_msg`, `smu_cmn_send_smc_msg_with_param`), `renoir_ppt.c` (the mailbox registers) and `smu_v12_0_ppsmc.h` (`0x1E`), with AMD's copyright and permission notice. The accelerant's copy in `gfx9_start.cpp` is not called; it stays the reset-on-init step inside the ring start, so the restart sends mode 2 a second time as part of that unchanged start. `r5_gfx9_kernel_restart()` runs `r5_gfx9_prepare` and `r5_gfx9_start` unchanged, then K1 and K2 as at boot. K1 keeps the handler and MSI vector from boot; K2 deletes its old system area before the new one. `r5_gfx9_after_restart()` sets the new user fence to the last sequence handed out. No register, PTE flag, invalidate word, ring content or firmware of a fixed section changed.

**Fault line (AFTER-M8 item 11).** `radeon_hd: vm fault vmid <n> addr <hex> status <hex>`, at most once per second, with `VM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_STATUS` of the GFX hub read after one dummy read and bit 0 of `VM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_CNTL` set, as in Linux `gmc_v9_0.c:656-665` and `675-676` (Linux leaves that bit set too). The M5 pasid lines stay one per fault (check-user reads them per VMID).

**Review fixes (PR 4222 review).** Mistakes found in the first version and fixed: (1) the restart could touch the chip before it was back: the reset now keeps the PCI header, clears bus mastering, sends the SMU message, writes the header back and waits for `RCC_CONFIG_MEMSIZE` to read other than `0xffffffff`, the frame of Linux v6.12 `amdgpu_device.c:5188-5242`; (2) the stale end-of-pipe drain had changed the boot K1, now only the restart does it; (3) the reset and restart ran up to about 4 s with the GPU lock held in the retire thread, so `GET_INFO`, close and app_server blocked: the lock is dropped and every other path that can reach the chip waits on `sResetting` (`gpu_wait_reset`, also after each wait inside a call and in close), and the SMU poll sleeps after the first millisecond; (4) the file VMID manager was set back to empty at REOPEN while lost files still held trees: owners now stay and every slot flushes on its next use (`r5_vmid_after_reset`, host case); (5) the one-second gate also hid the M5 pasid fault lines; (6) the self-test printed a second `mark selftest ok` without ms; (7) parked buffers were freed at the hang while the hung CP could still read them; now they are freed after a restart that worked (the hub must be programmed for the page-table writes), or at OFF when that hang's reset worked; after a second hang or a failed reset they stay allocated until reboot; (8) the fault register write is now cited and in the draft contract; (9) the `gpu_hang_test` pages were not freed at OFF, now they are (the hang word set to 1 first). Own review after these fixes: a restart whose K1 failed counted as ok, now it fails; a wrong self-test read-back now logs `mark selftest readback <hex>`. Review by the stick-tooling session: a failed restart was reported as `selftest failed`, now `reset failed` with no self-test line (policy case); the two interrupt-off writes before the reset are now in the draft contract; the fault status is read and cleared only for a printed line (the second fault printed 0, and a storm did three MMIO accesses per fault); a file that was guilty in a first hang stayed guilty after it destroyed its context, now lost and guilty clear together and the global guilty file is cleared at REOPEN.

**`gpu_hang_test <n>`** (test switch, off): armed by the self-test's last call (`R5_GPU_IH_COUNTS`), then the retire thread submits n jobs one after another, each a `WAIT_REG_MEM` on a GTT dword that stays 0 (`r5_hang_ib.h`, in `scripts/check-pm4.py`).

**`scripts/test-r5-gpu` (AFTER-M8 item 12).** The invalidation-range text now matches (three tabs, as in the file). ## 2026-11-12 - Kernel panic when joining a WPA network: the link domain has no address module (build 10060)

Stick 50 (`d6b2471ed4`, sha256 `177cbd31…`): the NetworkStatus menu no longer crashes, the network list shows, and joining "Skynet" with a password got through association. Then the kernel stopped in KDL (photo): `PANIC: vm_page_fault: unhandled page fault in kernel space at 0xb0`, thread `wpa_supplicant thread`, in `get_interface_address()` ← `datalink_is_local_address()` ← `datalink_send_routed_data()` ← `socket_send()` ← `sendto` from `wpa_supplicant` `l2_packet_send()` ← `wpa_supplicant_send_2_of_4()`: message 2 of the WPA 4-way handshake. The syslog on disk ends before the join; the KDL screen is the evidence.

Cause: an R5 change in `datalink_send_routed_data()` (from the IPv6 work, in `distro/rest/.../network/stack/datalink.cpp`) also asks `datalink_is_local_address(address->domain, buffer->destination)` for every routed send. wpa_supplicant sends its EAPOL frames through the link domain (`AF_LINK`), which is registered without an address module (`register_domain(AF_LINK, "link", NULL, NULL, …)`), and the address table hashes through that module. Nothing on R5 had sent link-level frames before this round. Fix (MIT snippet): the check runs only for a domain that has an address module; IP and IPv6 keep it. The `stack` module builds; not booted yet.

Review of all R5 changes in the network stack (`datalink.cpp`, `interfaces.cpp`, `routes.cpp` against Haiku), after this panic: the same NULL module could be reached by any caller of `get_interface_address()` with an `AF_LINK` address, including Haiku's own ioctl paths, because the address table's `HashKey()` checked for an unknown family but not for a domain without an address module. It now hashes such a key like an unknown family (MIT snippet in `interfaces.cpp`); `Compare()` already rejects a different family, so the lookup finds nothing. The other R5 changes were checked and are fine: the IPv6 source-address choice takes and drops references correctly (`Interface::AddressAt()` acquires one), `get_buffer_route()` is only reached for IP domains (Haiku's own code there already uses the address module), the route match checks `mask_address()`'s result, and the default-route fallback only runs with a route that has an interface address. The `stack` module builds; not booted yet.

## 2026-11-12 - Boot panic on the 5625U: the idle module was swapped under running CPUs (build 10060)

Stick 48 (build 10060, `873776597e`) stopped at boot in the kernel debugger: `PANIC: SMEP violation user-mapped address 0xffffffff8255cc90 touched from kernel`, thread `main2`, CPU 7. The stack: `cpu_init_post_modules` → `load_cpuidle_module` → `put_module` → `unload_kernel_add_on` → `vm_delete_area` → `X86VMTranslationMap::Flush` → `x86_cstates_text + 0xc90`. The other CPUs already run when the cpuidle modules are loaded. `load_cpuidle_module()` installed the first module it found (`x86_cstates`, rank 0.8) at once, then found `x86_acpi_cstates` (0.9), put the first one and unloaded its code while CPUs were idling in it; the TLB shootdown waited in `cpu_wait()` through the old module. The fault on the freed text is reported as SMEP.

Why now: on stick 47 `x86_acpi_cstates` refused (wrong ACPI processor ids), so only one module was ever installed. The MADT fix (`30da1eeda2`, PR #4212, on `main`) made the ACPI module valid, and that exposed this. air/OS fixed exactly this in `3683cfbe47` ("kernel: choose the cpuidle and cpufreq modules before using one"), merged together with the MADT and ACPI-idle commits as one set (`b5ea454b46`, "idle module selection, MADT processor IDs, x86_acpi_cstates"). R5 took two of the three. Mistake: the dependency check for this round looked at the network and Bluetooth layers and not again at the kernel set from #4212.

Change: `distro/kernel/src/system/kernel/cpu.cpp` with `3683cfbe47` (jmgasper, MIT): the best cpuidle and cpufreq module is chosen first, the others are put before anyone uses them, and only then is the chosen one published (`using cpuidle module <name>`). `scripts/apply-kernel-bugs.py` copies it.

`main` is affected too since #4212: a machine whose firmware gives `x86_acpi_cstates` valid processors panics at boot. QEMU never takes this path (no `_CST`), which is why the QEMU boots passed. Tested: kernel builds; not booted on the 5625U yet.

## 2026-11-12 - R5's own code is MIT

Problem: R5's own code was GPL-3.0-or-later, with MIT only for libraries and public headers. The other Haiku-based systems (air/OS, RenkuOS, haiku-pi) are MIT, and RenkuOS takes MIT only, so they could not use R5's fixes, while R5 takes theirs. R5's GPL snippets also sat inside `libbe` sources (`Alert.cpp`, `Button.cpp`, `Box.cpp` and others).

What changed: by the rights holder's decision, MIT is now the default for all new R5 code, and R5's existing code is relicensed to MIT. 421 files under `distro/`, `docs/`, `scripts/` and `tools/` had their SPDX identifier, their snippet identifiers or their "R5OS modifications" notice changed; no code line changed. The apply scripts that recognise an already copied file by that notice now match both the old and the new text. `AGENTS.md`, `docs/LICENSING.md` (new section "The change of 12 Nov 2026"), `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `README.md`, the website and the About Licenses text (`distro/about/licenses.txt`) say MIT.

Rights: every commit in those directories is from the R5 accounts, with Cursor and Claude as co-authors. The haiku-pi blocks (Witold Bołt) and air/OS blocks (jmgasper) were changes to Haiku's MIT files with no other license stated, so they are marked MIT again with their authors' copyright. The Linux `amdgpu` files the GPU code follows were checked in Linux v6.12: all carry the MIT permission text.

Not changed: the VirtualBox Guest Additions (GPL-3.0-only) and the R5 artwork and brand files (`distro/artwork/`, `r5_disk_badge.h`, `scripts/generate-r5-artwork.py`), which stay GPL-3.0-or-later until the rights holder decides. Builds published before this change keep their GPL-3.0-or-later offer. This history file is not rewritten.

## 2026-11-12 - CPU topology, scheduler and deep idle from air/OS (build 10059)

Stick 47 (the 14:58 anyboot of `110b185145`, sha256 `54829e08…`), one boot on the 5625U, logs in `generated/boot-5625u-47/syslog`:

- SMT topology works on hardware. `R5 CPU topology: leaf1 ebx 0x000c0800 80000008 ecx 0x0000400b 8000001e ebx 0x00000100 smt mask 0x1 core mask 0xe`. CPUs 0–11 are cores 0–5 with `smt` 0 and 1, and each pair has the same L1/L2 id (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). `scheduler_init: found 12 logical cpus and 3 cache levels`. Before (stick 33) every CPU was its own core.
- Deep idle did not switch on. `x86_acpi_cstates` was tried and refused: `can't find matching cpu_ent for acpi cpu 0` … `14`, `acpi cpu 15 maps to cpu 0`, `can't use x86 ACPI idle: missing 11 processor objects`. Then `using x86 C-States: C0, C1` as before. Cause: the MADT lists absent processors with APIC id 0, so the boot CPU took ACPI id 15, and the other CPUs reset their ACPI id when they set up their local APIC, after the MADT was read. air/OS fixed exactly this in `30da1eeda2b5e7d5d49d28b7ebcd95305b54e5df` (jmgasper, MIT: only enabled MADT entries, x2APIC entries too, the reset moved before the MADT read), which belongs with their ACPI idle commits and was missed in the first import. It is now taken: `apic.cpp` and `ioapic.cpp` in `distro/kernel`, copied by `scripts/apply-kernel-bugs.py`. `jam -q kernel_x86_64` builds with no warnings in those files. Not on a stick yet; deep idle stays unproven until the next 5625U boot.
- The owner saw no problems in the desktop, media, USB audio/MIDI and Device Manager tests, but could not check everything. Tracker takes 10–20 s to respond after the desktop appears, on every stick so far, so it is not from this change. The syslog has no timestamps; around Tracker's start the first-login Deskbar script and the MIDI and serial driver scans run. (The USB device that leaves and returns on hub port 1 at that time is the tester changing devices, not a fault.) Not diagnosed.
- `scripts/read-stick-logs.py` did not work elevated: it passed `> log 2>&1` to ShellExecute, which has no shell, so argparse got them as arguments (exit 2); and it read the raw disk at offsets that are not whole sectors (`read failed`). Now the elevated run writes its own log (`--log`, hidden), and raw reads cover whole 512-byte sectors. It numbered the folder 24 because only 23 is checked out here; renamed to 47.

Findings 1 and 6 of `docs/reviews/KERNEL-AMD64-REVIEW.md`, and `docs/KERNEL.md` findings 5 and 6, taken from air/OS instead of written again (`docs/ROADMAP.md`, "Other Haiku forks as sources"). Generic: every AMD Zen generation, Zen 5c, Intel hybrid cores, any x86 machine whose ACPI firmware has `_CST`. Not specific to the 5625U.

Problem: on AMD Zen, `detect_amd_cpu_topology()` read CPUID `0x80000008` ECX[15:12] as the core width, and the CmpLegacy bit then made every logical CPU a core. Stick 33 shows `smt 0` on all twelve CPUs of the 5625U while the L1/L2 ids come in six pairs, so the scheduler had twelve one-thread cores and could put two busy threads on one physical core while another core idled. Idle: `x86_cstates` builds its states from CPUID leaf 5, which on AMD lists C1 only (stick 33: `using x86 C-States: C0, C1`). AMD's deep core state is in ACPI `_CST`. `x86_acpi_cstates` was built but not in the image, and only handled Intel firmware.

What changed (all air/OS, jmgasper, MIT, cherry-picked onto the R5 files in that order; full hashes in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`):

- `1376a518e2` the scheduler uses idle cores; `7abf76e985` `cpu_ent::capacity` (larger is faster, 0 unknown) and the scheduler prefers the faster cores, set on x86 for Intel hybrid cores (P 1024, E 600); `71eadca3af`, `a4ddc48124`, `f100985748`, `3fbd41c840`, `1aa18e8aa5`, `10c5b544a8`, `f1d9347032`, `417666ae77`, `c3de7f3ac6`: placement on SMT and faster cores in low-latency and power-saving mode, and the fixes those changes needed.
- `49eda6ac00` Zen and later (family `0x17`+, leaf `0x8000001E` present): threads per core from `0x8000001E` EBX[15:8], the topology id from its EAX, the core width as logical width divided by threads per core. The `0x8000001D` cache sharing is no longer multiplied by the SMT threads (it already counts them). Zen 5 parts with Zen 5c cores (CPUID `0x80000026`) give those cores capacity 768. Older AMD keeps the old path.
- `2c48d1ae0c`, `32a4200329`, `e24004dc25` `x86_acpi_cstates`: ACPI0007 processor devices, `_OSC`/`_PDC` optional, AMD FFH and no ARB_DIS/BM_RLD on Zen, idle with interrupts disabled instead of a callback and `longjmp()`, the state chosen by a per-CPU running average of the idle time, deep states also in low-latency mode once idle periods last ten times the exit latency. On AMD with a state deeper than C1 it ranks above `x86_cstates`; elsewhere `x86_cstates` stays the module that is used.
- `scripts/apply-kernel-bugs.py` copies the new files from `distro/kernel` and adds `x86_acpi_cstates` before `x86_cstates` in the image (an idempotent hook, as for `i2c_hid`).
- R5's own: one syslog line on CPU 0, `R5 CPU topology: leaf1 ebx … 80000008 ecx … 8000001e ebx … smt mask … core mask …`, so a boot log shows what the masks were built from (SPDX-Snippet, GPL-3.0-or-later).

Not taken, and why: the arm64 and device-tree parts of `7abf76e985` (air/OS has its own arm64 base and the hunks do not apply; arm64 CPUs keep capacity 0, which the scheduler treats as all alike; ARM64 is parked). The clamp to `kMaxLoad` in `CoreEntry::GetLoad()` from `71eadca3af` comes from an earlier air/OS commit that R5 does not have; the zero-CPU check is taken, the clamp not. RenkuOS `cpu_block_deep_idle()` (a driver holding the CPUs out of deep idle) is a later step: it changes the same `acpi_cpuidle.cpp` and needs a merge by hand. air/OS `9f9dec61a` (profiler timer) touches `scheduler.cpp` but is unrelated and not taken.

Limits: the air/OS measurements are from a Threadripper 1950X, a Ryzen 7640U and a Ryzen AI 5 340, not from R5. What the 5625U firmware puts in `_CST` is not known yet. Intel hybrid and Zen 5c are not tested on R5 (no such machine). ARM64 not built.

Tested: `jam -q kernel_x86_64 x86_acpi_cstates x86_cstates` in WSL, no warnings in the changed files. From an LF clone of this branch in WSL (`110b185145`): `scripts/apply-overlay.sh` exit 0, `x86_acpi_cstates` once in the package list; `scripts/jam-r5-raw.sh` `jam_exit=0`, `mesa_exit=0`, `mesa_packages_ok`; `jam -q @r5-anyboot` exit 0 (2156724224 bytes, 14:58). QEMU TCG, image as a snapshot, 1 socket × 2 cores × 2 threads, two boots, no panic, the second reached the R5 welcome screen (screendump):

- `-cpu qemu64`: `R5 CPU topology: leaf1 ebx 0x00040800 80000008 ecx 0x00002003 8000001e ebx 0x00000000 smt mask 0x0 core mask 0x3`; not Zen, so the old AMD path, four CPUs with `smt 0`, as before.
- `-cpu EPYC-Rome,+topoext`: leaf `0x8000001E` EBX is `0x100` (two threads per core), but TCG does not offer `topoext` in leaf `0x80000001` (QEMU warns), so the Zen path correctly stands back and the masks are the old ones. The Zen path itself was not exercised: this WSL has no KVM.
- `no valid cpuidle module found` on both: QEMU's firmware has no `_CST` and its CPU model no MWAIT C-states, so neither module loads. Not a test of deep idle.

Not tested: the Zen path, deep idle, Zen 5c and Intel hybrid on hardware. That is the 5625U stick (SMT ids inside the six L1 pairs, which cpuidle module is found, the `_CST` states, a responsive desktop after idle).

## 2026-11-12 - media_server and Media fixes from the review

All points of `docs/reviews/MEDIA-SERVER-REVIEW.md` (#4207). No What's new section; `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

media_server (`DefaultManager`): when the output node is gone, the mixer is disconnected through the roster (that also tells the producer when the consumer is dead, so the mixer frees its one output) and `fTimeSource` is cleared, so the next card gets a live time source. `_ConnectMixerToOutput()` checks `GetTimeSource()` before `SetTimeSourceFor()`. `Set(AUDIO_OUTPUT)` clears the fallback flag before its early return, so choosing the device that stands in is saved. `SaveState()` makes what it writes the saved default in memory (`fMsgList`); `NodeManager` calls it after every `Set()`, so a device chosen in this session is the one the rescan restores. `fMsgList` and the fallback flags are behind a lock, and `_FindPhysical()` works on a copy. Video defaults also go back to the saved device. A "None" node that stands in no longer replaces the saved device. Two devices with the same name are logged when the name match picks one.

media_addon_server: the flavor rescan runs on the application looper (posted from the control thread), because it changes `fInfoMap` and `active_flavors`, which the looper also changes. Nodes that are gone are dropped from `active_flavors` before adding one and before the add-on is put, and a node is not added twice. A live instance only counts as present when its name matches the flavor; after an unplug the next card can take the flavor id that an old node still has. (Correction to review point 8: a stale entry does not cost the 50 ms wait at quit; `StopNode()` fails first and the loop skips it.)

Media kit: `NotificationManager` returns when a request has no valid node, instead of copying from an uninitialized pointer.

Media preferences: every node reference that Media takes is released (`_GetNode()` says when; a node Media instantiates itself is kept, as `SetAudioOutput(dormant_node_info)` does); the four default `Get*()` calls in the window were never released either. Choosing the marked device sends the choice again. A burst of `B_MEDIA_FLAVORS_CHANGED` gives one refresh after 300 ms, and the default menus are shown again 1.5 s later, after media_server's rescan; `ML_UPDATE_DEFAULTS` only updates the default menus. The latency, layout and surround files are read and written by one helper: the whole file is read (up to 1 MB; a larger file is left alone), and written to a temporary file that is renamed. Reading creates nothing. They go to `/boot/home/config/settings/kernel/drivers`, the directory the kernel reads (`kUserSettingsDirectory`) and media_addon_server reads; before, a standard account wrote its own home and nothing read it. Those three menus are gray for an account that cannot write there, and the USB layout menu is gray without a USB sound card (`/dev/audio/hmulti/usb`). A failed save marks the saved value again, and a failed `usb_audio` latency write puts `hda.settings` back. The "Restart media services" hint appears after a change, not from the start. The duplicate `AllAttached()` is gone. R5 parts carry SPDX-Snippet GPL-3.0-or-later tags (also the older latency, layout and surround code).

Administrator lock for those three menus: a standard account sees a lock button next to the hint (the same `r5_button_set_lock()` as Settings). Unlocking asks for an administrator password (`r5_admin_prompt_unlock()`); then Login writes the file (`kMsgAdminSetDriverSetting`, `'r5ds'`, `distro/login/DriverSettingsAdmin.cpp`). Login checks the grant and accepts only `hda.settings`, `usb_audio` and `virtual_surround` with the Latency, USB layout and Virtual surround keys and values; any other file, key or value is refused, so it cannot write an arbitrary file as uid 0. The file code moved from Media to `libr5ui.so` (`DriverSettings.cpp`, MIT, `r5_driver_settings_read/write/writable()` and `r5_admin_set_driver_setting()`, added at the end of `AdminLock.h`, `docs/LIBR5.md`), so Media and Login share it. Media now links `libr5ui.so` and `libr5icons.so` (`distro/media/src/preferences/media/Jamfile`, Haiku's plus those two). The lock follows the 5-minute grant (checked every 15 s and after a failed save). An administrator gets no lock button and writes directly. Not `BAdminLockBar`: that disables every view in the window, and the rest of Media is personal.

Limits: a USB card plugged in while Media is open does not enable the USB layout menu until Media is opened again. Two identical cards still match the first by name. The flavor-name check cannot tell two cards with the same name apart. A file Login wrote is owned by uid 0; the administrator can still replace it, because Media writes a temporary file and renames it in a directory the administrator owns.

## 2026-11-12 - The open points of the USB audio and MIDI review (build 10058)

The smaller points left open in build 10057 (`docs/reviews/USB-AUDIO-MIDI2-REVIEW.md`, status section).

Unplug (`usb_midi`): a port that is open when the device is unplugged, and the device while any of its ports is open, are no longer freed under the program. `usb_midi_removed` cancels the transfers, takes the ports off the list, wakes a blocked reader, and frees only what is not open. `usb_midi_free` frees the rest with the last cookie (`open_count`, `removed`). `usb_midi_open` refuses a removed device. Remaining window: Haiku's `search_port_info` returns a port without holding the list lock, so an open that races the unplug itself is not covered (that is `devlist.cpp`, not changed here).

Bus speed: the USB bus manager answers `usb_ioctl(B_USB_IOCTL_GET_DEVICE_SPEED)` with the device's speed (new MIT header `<usb/R5USBSpeed.h>`, values checked against `usb_speed` at compile time; `usb.cpp` copied into `distro/kernel` and added to `apply-kernel-bugs.py`). The module structure is unchanged; an older stack returns `B_DEV_INVALID_IOCTL` and `usb_audio` falls back to the guess. Before, every UAC 2.0 device was taken for high speed.

`usb_audio`: the silence put in for a missed record packet is counted in `fPadded` and logged once per second of it. `_QueryClockRates` gives the clock's rates only to alternates whose terminal runs from that clock.

Not changed, after a look: the recording carry. It can hold almost a whole buffer, but that is audio, not drift: after a short capture is held back, the next transfer brings two buffers. A cap of 4 ms dropped most of a buffer on a slow device clock; `test-usb-audio-packets` failed (`44100 Hz drift -1: buffer 2 frame 176 is 880, want 617`) and the cap was taken out again. The latency is at most one buffer; a smaller buffer in Media lowers it. The review point was wrong on that.

MIDI 1.0 devices stay MIDI 1.0 bytes through `midi_server`: handing them over as UMP would change what an existing program's `Data()` receives. Documented in `docs/MIDI2.md` (Limits), with the `UMP1` marker.

Manufacturer ID: R5 itself never presents itself to a MIDI device; only `midi2test` and the fuzzer use the kit's catalogs. The identity is the program's: new `<Midi2Identity.h>` (`midi2_identity`, `B_MIDI2_NONCOMMERCIAL_ID`), `midi2_pe_catalog_set_identity` (writes DeviceInfo, refuses 8-bit bytes and names that would need JSON escaping) and `midi2_endpoint_set_identity`, added at the end of `libmidi2.so`; the existing calls are unchanged and still default to `0x7D`. So R5 does not buy a SysEx ID now; `docs/ROADMAP.md` keeps the item for the case that R5 ships its own MIDI 2.0 device. `midi2test` checks the new calls (built, not run); the same checks passed in a host build with ASan/UBSan, and `fuzz-midi2` property and stream ran 60 s `ok`.

Licensing: the R5 UMP code in `usb_midi.cpp` and `usb_midi.h` is inside SPDX snippet tags (20 in the source file, no code changed by the tagging; the 3 Nov entry said they were there).

Tested: `jam -q usb usb_audio usb_midi` in WSL, no warnings (`-Werror`). Host: `test-usb-audio-packets` and `test-usb-midi-sysex` `ok`, `fuzz-midi2 kernel` 60 s `ok` with ASan/UBSan. No image, no boot, no USB sound card or MIDI device; unplug and the speed request are not run.

Stick 47 (build 10059, 12 Nov 2026, 5625U): unplug while open now runs on hardware. A Pioneer DDJ-1000 (AlphaTheta `2b73:0020`) was plugged in, opened by `midi_server` (`usb_midi_open … open (1)`), and pulled out three times. Each time: `usb_midi_removed`, `usb_midi_read: loop terminated -- Device no longer active`, `usb_midi_close`, `usb_midi_free`, `remove_port … done`, `remove_device`, and no panic; plugging it in again published `midi/usb/0/0` anew. The DDJ-1000's audio interface is vendor-specific (class 255), not USB Audio Class, so `usb_audio` correctly leaves it (`Ignore interface of unsupported subclass 0x3` is its MIDI streaming interface). The owner saw no problem with USB sound; the full-speed rate and the bus-speed request do not show in the syslog and are not confirmed.

## 2026-11-12 - USB audio and MIDI fixes from the review (build 10057)

Points 2 to 16 of `docs/reviews/USB-AUDIO-MIDI2-REVIEW.md`, and three of its smaller points. Point 1 was #4203.

MIDI over USB (`usb_midi`): a MIDI 2.0 device is switched to the alternate whose MS header says `bcdMSC 0x0200` (`set_alt_interface`); before, alternate 0 (MIDI 1.0) always stayed active and the UMP code never ran on a real device. The Group Terminal Blocks are read with `GET_DESCRIPTOR` (`0x26`, alternate, interface), header first, as Linux does; one port per group, group 1 only when they cannot be read. The protocol is taken from the Stream Configuration Notification (`0x006`), not the Request (`0x005`). An interrupt OUT endpoint is queued as interrupt. `CINcode`: `0xF1` (MTC) is CIN 0x2 and `0xF6` CIN 0x5 (both wrong in Haiku as well). The UMP walk steps over reserved message types instead of dropping the rest of the transfer. `Midi2Usb.h`: a Group Terminal Block is subtype `0x02`; `0x01` is the header (`B_MIDI2_USB_GROUP_TERMINAL_HEADER_SUBTYPE`). Development builds up to 10056 used `0x01`.

MIDI 2.0 kit: `BMidiLocalConsumer` passes UMP type 0x1 (clock, start, stop, continue, time code, song position, song select) to MIDI 1.0 hooks. MIDI-CI catalogs get a random 28-bit MUID instead of 1; the family and endpoint name are `R5`. `midi2_pe_header_number` refuses a value above 2^31 − 1 instead of overflowing. The manufacturer ID stays `0x7D` (educational use) until R5 has its own.

USB audio (`usb_audio`): buffer exchange waits at most one second, so a stream that was stopped from another thread (format or latency change) no longer leaves the media add-on waiting forever. (The review said the error stop after 32 transfers caused that hang; it does not, because the callback releases the semaphore once before it stops.) `Start()` resets the buffer cycle, the processed count and both carries. `B_MULTI_SET_ENABLED_CHANNELS` writes back only the card's bytes. `B_MULTI_GET_DESCRIPTION` returns zeroed spare entries. `B_MULTI_GET_BUFFERS` returns a stream's error and puts each stream at its own channel offset (also Haiku code). A rate change on a UAC 2.0 clock that another running stream uses returns `B_BUSY` and changes nothing; before, it set up buffers for the new rate and reported success. Feedback: a value is used only within 1/8 of nominal, a full-speed 16.16 value is recognised, an error no longer stops the feedback, a failed queue paces at nominal, and the extra frame is limited by `wMaxPacketSize` instead of being clamped off. The product name is UTF-8. A successful rate change is logged as information.

Not done: the unplug use-after-free in `usb_midi` (Haiku design), `B_MIDI_READ_UMP` on a MIDI 1.0 device, the bus-speed guess, the recording carry size, the SPDX snippet tags on the older UMP code in `usb_midi.cpp`.

Tested: `jam -q usb_midi usb_audio libmidi2.so midi2test midi_server` in WSL, no warnings (`-Werror`). Host: `fuzz-midi2` targets kernel, payload, property, profile, stream and usb, 60 s each with AddressSanitizer and UBSan, all `ok`; `test-usb-midi-sysex` and `test-usb-audio-packets` `ok`. No image was built and nothing was booted; no USB sound card and no MIDI device was attached. `midi2test` was built but not run.

## 2026-11-12 - Device Manager, and the administrator lock in libr5ui

Haiku's Devices app lists the kernel device tree but is hard to use. Device Manager (`distro/apps/devicemanager`, Build 10056) works like Windows 11 Device Manager: devices by type or by connection, a status badge, Properties with General, Driver, Details and Events, turning a driver off and on, Action > Turned-off drivers, and File > Export as full details or as a tree. Devices stays installed. The whole app is MIT. It builds Haiku's Devices code unchanged from `src/apps/devices`. Details: `docs/DEVICE-MANAGER.md`.

Which driver serves a device: the kernel's driver path, then a legacy `reserve_device()` node (HDA, FreeBSD network drivers), then a `/dev/graphics/<driver>_BBDDFF` name, then the bus driver below a controller (`busses/ata`, `busses/usb`, `busses/virtio`) and the function driver below that. The nodes in between are hidden unless Show hidden devices, in their device's group.

The administrator lock (`AdminLock.*`) was GPL-3.0-or-later and compiled into Settings, Users, Time, Screen, Network, Printers, Repositories and VirtualMemory. Mistakes found in QEMU and fixed before this entry: controllers served by a `busses/` driver showed "No driver" and their helper nodes filled Other devices; watching `/dev` did not report a USB keyboard, so the window now compares the node ids every 2 seconds; a long device name pushed the Properties buttons out of a fixed-size window, so the window is resizable and long values truncate.

## 2026-11-12 - MIDI input works again; MIDI Monitor (build 10055)

Problem: no MIDI input reached any program. A Pioneer DDJ-1000 gave no input in R5 while it works on Windows. `MidiPortProducer::GetData()` in `midi_server` compared the return value of `ioctl(fd, B_MIDI_READ_UMP, ...)` with `B_UNSUPPORTED`, `B_DEV_INVALID_IOCTL` and `B_TIMED_OUT`. The icon is the Haiku MIDI server icon, unchanged.

Limits: the other review points (MIDI 2.0 over USB, `usb_midi` table errors, unplug while reading) are not in this change. Whether the DDJ-1000 is bound by `usb_midi` at all is not known: that needs its USB descriptors or a syslog from a boot with it attached.

Tested: see the pull request. No MIDI device was attached during this work.

## 2026-11-12 - Quiet the USB lines from the 5625U boot

The vanilla stick boot logged four USB lines that are not faults.

An isochronous transfer event can arrive after its transfer was already finished: the event-data completion, or the stop when CodyCam quits. xHCI no longer logs that retired TRB as an error. `cancel queued transfers` is not logged when the endpoint has nothing queued.

A default USB alternate with `wMaxPacketSize` 0 is not a configured endpoint. xHCI still refuses it, and does not log it.

## 2026-11-11 - USB isochronous transfers on xHCI

RenkuOS group A, applied onto our copies. Group B is the section above.

Taken:

- `3f4ee2d0facb1d8cd0a04a3938f4185358408d26` (David Beckman). An isochronous transfer used one buffer per packet, each the size of the largest packet, while each TRB only sent that packet's own length. A short packet left a gap, and the next packet read the wrong bytes. 44.1 kHz alternates packet sizes. The packets now share one buffer, and each TRB starts where the previous one ended. Bulk and interrupt transfers are unchanged.
- `942e51e6d6295bf24c28ec0c36806a5256509ebf` and `dc8872b9823656b7b323821cffc4d998970735d2` (Bryan Irvine), as one change. A VIA VL805 reads past the last TRB. We already left 4 empty TRBs on every controller (haiku-pi `c65ac5a2e6`). That is now 32 empty TRBs, and only when the controller is a VL805 (PCI 1106:3483). Other controllers, including both test laptops, get no pad. The kernel debugger still hands out 128-byte chunks: the pad is off on these machines, so a TD still fits. The ACPI `_CCA` test in `dc8872b982` was not added. This driver is the PCI driver, and the VL805 id is in the PCI header. A VL805 on AMD64 would not fit a padded TD in the kernel debugger.
- `8d6303031ecf2800fdcef718646644ec1b674b67` (David Beckman). When a queued isochronous transfer names a frame that has already passed, xHCI and OHCI used that frame anyway, and the next transfer chained from it, so the stream stayed late. If the frame is not safely ahead, the driver now starts from the controller's frame plus a margin and writes that frame back. OHCI uses the 16-bit frame and a margin of 5. xHCI uses the isochronous scheduling threshold and a margin of at least 5. The message is logged at most once every 10 seconds. `ohci.cpp` is now one of our copies. UHCI already had this guard.

Already in R5, so not applied again:

- `5b6210a165` (reset a stalled endpoint). `FinishTransfers` already resets a control pipe on any error and a bulk or interrupt pipe on a stall, through air/OS `bdad03ac62`.
- `4214bdbe4b` and `300b6c30de` (descriptor length). `Device.cpp` already rejects a descriptor shorter than 2 bytes or past the buffer, and shortens `total_length` when the configuration is shorter than that field. `300b6c30de` is Haiku `d1111656df`.
- `0a6da2e43c` (SuperSpeed companion before an endpoint). `Device.cpp` already drops that companion.
- `80c55f2ef4` (allocator waiter count and a slot check). Our allocator has no waiter count, and it checks the slot while holding its lock.
- `7637e637e4` and `ca923659b4` (bandwidth arithmetic). `Transfer.cpp` in the tree already uses a 32-bit count and adds the high-speed term. The file was not copied.
- `b6060b0ddb` (half a second, and a last success must not panic). `Object::WaitForIdle` already waits half a second and checks the reference count after the loop. The two-second wait was not taken.

## 2026-11-11 - Review of the audio branch: overflow and build fixes

The audio branch had not been built. A review found: `Stream::GetEnabledChannels()` set bits past the 16-byte kernel bitmap once all streams of a device had more than 128 channels (64 per stream is allowed), so a large device overwrote the kernel stack. The streams now stop at `kMaxEnabledChannels` (128). The driver copied all 16 bytes of the bitmap to and from the caller; a Haiku caller sizes it for its own channels, so it now copies `(channels + 7) / 8` bytes. The playback feedback error had no limit and could wrap its `int32` after about an hour with a fast device clock; it is capped at four frames. With the 8-frame carry full, holding one more frame back dropped one; that step now waits. The starting frame of the feedback transfer is a member instead of a stack variable.

Build fixes: `Device.cpp` compared a `uint8` with 256 and `NULL` with a `usb_device` id; `memcpy` into Media Kit classes needs a `void*` cast under GCC 13. The R5 UAC 2.0 clock code moved into `ProgramClock()` without its SPDX snippet; the snippet is back. The ported RenkuOS changes keep their MIT credit lines and are not marked as R5 snippets.

Tested: every changed `.cpp` compiles with the command line `jam -n` prints, `-Werror` included, from a copy outside the shared tree (Cursor was building there). Not jammed into an image, not booted, no USB audio or MIDI device.

## 2026-11-11 - Playback follows an explicit USB feedback endpoint

A playback interface that has a feedback endpoint now reads it and moves one frame per buffer into or out of a small carry, so the packets follow the device clock. The client's buffer is still one exact buffer; the extra frame comes from the carry, or one frame is held back. A device without that endpoint is queued as before, at the nominal packet size. Implicit feedback, using the capture stream as the clock, is not done. High speed is read as 16.16 frames per microframe, full speed as 10.14 frames per frame. Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A short USB recording waits for a full buffer

Each capture transfer used to become exactly one record buffer. What the device sent beyond that was dropped, and a short transfer was filled by repeating the last frame, so recording followed the host clock while playback followed the device. The extra frames now start the next buffer, and a short transfer is not published until the buffer is full. An empty packet, a service interval the host missed, is nominal silence, so the audio after it stays in time. The host test `scripts/test-usb-audio-packets.cpp` passed on this machine. Ported from RenkuOS `b3dc1212e4` (rations, MIT) onto the existing carry. Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - USB audio arms every stream before one starts

A UAC 2.0 device with playback and capture used to program each stream on its own. The second interface was then switched while the first was already running on the same clock, and a UMC204HD stays silent for as long as capture runs. On a fresh run the driver now parks every streaming interface, programs each clock once, selects the active alternates, and only then queues a transfer. A clock is not rewritten while another stream of that device is running. UAC 1.0 is unchanged. Ported from RenkuOS `a842555ed6` (rations, MIT) onto this driver's clock write. Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Buffer length stays on the Latency page

RenkuOS `6ed1b63f79` adds a Buffer size menu on the sound card and asks the driver for that many frames. That menu is not added. Media already writes `play_buffer_frames` and `record_buffer_frames`, and the USB driver reads them. HD Audio already reads the same file. A live control that sends a short buffer to HD Audio stops its interrupts, which is why that commit left HD Audio out. The request fields in `multi_audio` stay 0, so a driver keeps its own default unless it reads the Latency file itself. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A plugged-in sound card replaces the fallback

While a fallback stands in for a saved input or output, a rescan looks for that saved device again. When it has a node, the media server uses it and reconnects the mixer to the new output. The saved name is not overwritten. Ported from RenkuOS `e95a210256` (rations, MIT). Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Opening Media does not save the fallback device

Showing the current input or output also told the media server to set it. The server treats that as a choice, so a fallback for a missing USB card became the saved device, and choosing an output could put the input back on the built-in card. The menus now only mark the current default. A choice in the menu sets it, and creates the node first when the card appeared after the media services started. A failure is reported and the menus show the default in use. The latency menu and the USB layout menu are unchanged. Ported from RenkuOS `2aee4b6c3c` (rations, MIT). Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Media refreshes its device lists when a card appears

The Media preferences built the device lists when the window opened and when the media server started. A sound card plugged in while the window was open stayed invisible until Media was opened again. The window now watches flavor changes and rebuilds the lists. A restarted media server drops that watch, so it is renewed each time the server starts. A device that the driver still lists after it is unplugged stays in the list. Ported from RenkuOS `917e0e9e30` (rations, MIT). Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Media messages are copied before they are used

The node, source, destination and format in a media message are not aligned. The notification server and the parameter controls used them in place, which faults on ARM. They are copied out first. Ported from RenkuOS `cf12459a32` (atomozero, MIT). Not booted on ARM64. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A missing sound card does not erase the saved default

The media server matched a saved input or output on flavor id, name and add-on path together. The flavor id is only the device's place in the list, so one USB card that is absent at boot renumbers the others and the saved card was missed. A miss then left no output, and the next save stored the fallback in place of the preference. The server now matches the name from the same add-on when the id moved, and otherwise uses the first real device for this session while keeping the saved entry. An explicit choice in the Media preferences replaces that fallback. Plugging the card in later does not switch the mixer back yet. Ported from RenkuOS `d1028141c2` (rations, MIT). Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A node created on request is released at quit

The Media preferences can ask the add-on server to create a sound-card node. That node was not on the list the server releases when it quits, so restarting the media services unloaded the add-on under the node's thread. The control thread now tells the application looper, and the looper records the node with the others. A node that was already released is skipped, because stopping it fails. A node created while the quit is already running is still not recorded. Ported from RenkuOS `bc165f5613` (rations, MIT). Creating nodes for a card that appears later was already in this file. Not tested with a USB device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Media flavor data is copied before it is used

Flattened flavor info is packed, so the numbers after the strings are not aligned. On ARM the media server died at start with SIGBUS. The numbers are copied with `memcpy`, and the request buffers in the media server, the add-on server and `BMediaNode` are aligned to 8 bytes. Ported from RenkuOS `4b157fb134` (atomozero, MIT). Not booted on ARM64. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A short USB audio configuration does not panic

Replug indexed the remembered interface and alternate without checking that the new configuration has them. A missing alternate is a small non-NULL pointer, so the old NULL check never fired. The indexes are checked first. An alternate with no endpoint is skipped, the same way an alternate with no format already was. Adapted from RenkuOS `428e08cd07` (David Beckman, MIT). Not reproduced with a truncated descriptor. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Notices for the RenkuOS audio ports

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names the RenkuOS commits ported onto `usb_midi`, `multi_audio`, and `usb_audio`, and their authors. The files stay MIT. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A USB audio device uses its product name

Media listed every USB interface as "USB Audio". The description now uses the USB product string, and "USB Audio" when the device has none. Two units of the same model still share that name. Taken from the naming idea in the Media-OS driver, on our `Device`. No device was attached. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A USB audio stream may carry 64 channels

The parser, the alternate choice and the channel list stopped at 16. A stream may now carry 64. Channels past the eight named positions are stereo pairs. The description ioctl copies up to 128 channel entries from the heap, and the enable bitmap is 16 bytes so a channel past 31 is not written off a `uint32`. Set-enabled reads the caller's bits before it uses them. Adapted from RenkuOS `8d3c445d68` (rations, MIT). The description bound from `6dfd2fbc30` is included so the higher count does not overflow. Not opened on an 18-input interface. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - multi_audio holds 128 channels

The add-on stored 32 channels and built the enable mask with a shift of the channel count, which is undefined from 32. It now holds 128, refuses a device that does not fit, and uses one bit per channel in a byte map. A buffer list with more rows than the tables is refused. Adapted from RenkuOS `8db4b0d1b4` (rations, MIT). The driver still describes at most 16 channels until the next change. Not opened on a wide interface. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - An unplugged sound card keeps its place in the list

`multi_audio` already watches `/dev/audio/hmulti`. Removing a card used to leave it listed as if it were still there, and deleting the slot would renumber the others. A card that disappears stays in the list with its presence cleared, and plugging it in again takes a new slot. The flavor index does not move. Adapted from RenkuOS `cf885a005b` (David Beckman, MIT). Not checked by unplugging a device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - A sound card is only the directions it has

`multi_audio` listed every card as both an input and an output. A card with no capture channels is no longer an input, and a card with no playback channels is no longer an output. Ported from RenkuOS `bd571637d2` (David Beckman, MIT). Not checked in Media. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - The sound card ignores a burst of clock samples

At the start of a stream the driver reports several buffers a few microseconds apart. The time estimate jumped, and the mixer could wait until nothing played. Pairs closer than half a buffer period are ignored. The period comes from the playback buffer when nothing is recording. Ported from RenkuOS `303b85eae5` (David Beckman, MIT). Not played through a device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - multi_audio queues four input buffers

Each playback input held one buffer. A buffer that arrived while that slot was full was dropped, and the next beat was silence. The slot is now a queue of four. A full queue still waits 100 µs once and then drops the new buffer. Stopping the thread recycles what is still queued. Ported from RenkuOS `7405980fad` (David Beckman, MIT). Not played through a device. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - Roland and Edirol Advanced mode is a table

Those interfaces have no USB-MIDI descriptors, so the driver matches vendor 0x0582 and a per-model table of interface number and cable masks. A composite unit is found by its non-isochronous IN and OUT pair. An interrupt IN endpoint is queued as an interrupt transfer. The driver scans every endpoint for the first IN and the first OUT. A missing port in the middle of the cable list is skipped instead of ending the scan. Standard mode still uses the class descriptors. Ported from RenkuOS `cb61494f02` (David Beckman, MIT). No Roland device was attached. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

A Yamaha interface such as the UX-256 carries a normal MIDI header inside a vendor-specific interface, so `usb_midi` never matched it. Vendor 0x0499 is now accepted, and a non-audio interface with a MIDIStreaming header is used. When the endpoint descriptors do not name the cables, the jack descriptors are counted, at most 16 each. - `cb22fd5cfe`, idumych: an Elan clickpad reports a right click for two fingers or the bottom-right corner, and a middle click for three fingers.

## 2026-11-11 - The GPU back buffer uses the scanout pitch

The GPU back buffer reported `width * 4` bytes per row. On DCE 2 and later the framebuffer pitch is the width rounded up to a multiple of 64 pixels. A 1366-wide screen is 1408 pixels of stride, 5632 bytes against 5464. `GPUCopy::Copy` then latched `gpu copy off: pitch` for the session. The 5625U boots at 1920x1080, and 1920 is already a multiple of 64, so stick 41 did not take this path. The back buffer now takes the front buffer's bytes per row. The read-back compares the visible pixels and leaves the padding out. Not jammed and not booted. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.

## 2026-11-11 - The screen offset was the BAR, not the carveout

Stick 41 kept the desktop copy on the CPU. `R5_GPU_SCANOUT_BO` treated `frame_buffer_phys` as an address inside the carveout: it subtracted `MC_VM_FB_OFFSET << 24` and rejected the result when it fell outside the visible window. On the 5625U those are different bases. Earlier boots recorded the PCI BAR at `0xfce0000000` and `MC_VM_FB_OFFSET` `0x810`, so the carveout is `0x810000000`. The picture sits at the start of the BAR (`window +0x0`). The difference of the two bases is far past the 256 MiB window, so the call returned `B_ERROR` once. app_server logged `gpu copy off: scanout refused` and then stayed on the CPU. That one line was already rotated out of `syslog` and `syslog.1` by the `user job fence` lines `gpu_debug` prints for every submit. VirtualBox never opens `/dev/gpu/radeon_hd/0`, so this refusal cannot show up there.

The offset is now `frame_buffer_phys - vram_bar_phys`. The page tables still add the carveout base. A refusal logs the physical address, the BAR, and the mode. A success logs `scanout bar+<offset>`. While the copy stays off, each `copy cpu median` line repeats `gpu copy off: <reason>`. `check.sh` reads `syslog.1` and `syslog.old` as well as `syslog`. It keeps the text after the last boot welcome, and when that welcome is already gone it keeps the remaining log instead of an empty file. An empty excerpt no longer passes the negative lines. `gpu_debug` still logs every user submit, so a long session can still rotate the boot banner away. Not jammed and not booted. There is no What's new section and `distro/BUILD` stays the same.
